body.p: When the AI needs more details before it can continue, it asks you instead of guessing. The questions appear in the conversation, each with a set of suggested answers, and the AI waits for your reply before going any further.

Choose one of the suggested answers, or select Other... and type your own. A question that accepts more than one answer at a time shows its answers as check boxes instead of radio buttons. Nothing is final until you select Continue, which becomes available once every question has an answer. You can also answer by typing in the chat input box. In that case, what you type answers the first question that is still waiting for an answer.
If you would rather not answer, select Skip. The AI is told that you declined, decides on its own, and continues.
The whole box can be used from the keyboard: Tab moves between the answers, the arrow keys move between the choices for a single-answer question, Enter continues, and Esc skips.

The questions and the answers you gave remain part of the conversation, so they are shown again if you reopen it later from the history. A single question is labeled Question, while a set is labeled Questions followed by the number of questions. If you skipped instead of answering, the record simply shows Skipped.
